Dr. Heiden: Shut up. Wait, shit. Uh… forty-five minutes, twenty-three seconds. Oh, man. Terminating experiment, I may be compromised by SCP-641. *sounds of a chair scuffling* Stevens, replace the object in its holding container, I'm going to Psych for an evaluation.

See that? That is the striking image of a responsible researcher.

Wait, so if the doll is… say a 4 inch radius… that's only 50,000 layers and some change. Why haven't we set a D-class on it overnight and catalogued it all the way to the core? If we need him to stop for some reason, we don't say anything, a guard just shoots him in the back with a fast-acting tranq dart.

We could even videotape the disassembly with high-speed film. You know, just in case any of the layers show any… interesting artistic deviations. :)

item.content:encoded:
I really enjoyed this, especially as a means to pacify humanoids. I get a similar image of this as I do with SCP-555-J (I think that's it) where it says that episodes of The Deadliest Warriors kept Able preoccupied until he was recontained.

It also makes me respect Dr. Heiden for his self-discipline, which is cool.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think this could use a touch-up, but the effect itself and how it's presented are definitely good. Kind of unnerving on the whole, considering how easy it is to get distracted by trivial shit like this in real life.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This article is up for review, If you check it out I'll be your best friend.

This is a pretty boring compulsion object, in my humble opinion. The description is just one big ugly block of text, and while I did like the base effect I felt like it needed something more. The addenda are all unnecessary, ranging from bland to bad. In short, I think this is a neat idea done with pretty bleah execution. I'd love to see this one expanded upon.
